__README: PROJECT-LEVEL sandbox policy: the grants one project needs. Copy the
claude-settings.user.json, which carries the machine-wide restrictions.
Filesystem arrays MERGE across settings scopes rather than replacing
one another, so these entries ADD to the user-level rules instead of
overriding them. An edit during a session is applied to the running
session, so a path can be widened mid-task without restarting.

__NOTE_dot: '.' resolves to the PROJECT ROOT when the configuration lives in
project settings. In ~/.claude/settings.json the same '.' would
resolve to ~/.claude instead, which is why these entries belong
The working directory is writable by default; it is listed
explicitly so the intent is visible to whoever reads this file.

__NOTE_network: Opened here rather than at user level, so the hole is scoped to the
one project that pulls dependencies. Delete this block entirely for a
project that only builds and tests: an offline sandbox is the
stronger position and costs nothing when there is nothing to fetch.
__NOTE_mutable_env: To let the agent INSTALL into an environment, add the environment
prefix and the package cache to allowWrite above:
Name ONE environment, never the whole envs directory: a wider entry
lets a task for this project break another project's environment.
Without the pkgs entry a solve downloads and then fails to write,
which presents as a confusing permission error.
Better still, clone the real environment and grant write access only
to the clone, which is disposable:
DO NOT reach for sandbox.excludedCommands to make a build work. An
excluded command runs with your full access and no network proxy, and
a pattern covering an interpreter or a script inside the working
